CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an 88-year-old gentleman who presents with left arm pain that began approximately two weeks ago. He woke at 2:00 AM with severe pain in his hand and arm. He applied ice which provided some relief. He attempted positioning his arm down to improve circulation without benefit. The pain gradually eased around 4-5 AM. This pattern of nocturnal pain recurred over several nights. Pain starts in the hand and radiates down the entire arm. He reports associated weakness in his hand, particularly with gripping. He notes that if pain occurs at night, he typically experiences some discomfort the following day as well. He denies neck pain with head turning or shoulder discomfort. He was evaluated by another provider who suspected a pinched nerve and started him on numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin, which have provided some relief. He notes that for the last couple of nights his neck has not been bothering him, though his hand continues to cause discomfort. He also mentions a previous finger injury that does not function properly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for weakness except in hand gripping. Negative for neck pain with head movement or shoulder discomfort. Denies radicular pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Cervical arthritis with disc degeneration
2. Neuropathy affecting lower extremities
3. VA disability - 1% disabled related to knee and foot issues

MEDICATIONS
1. Gabapentin (dose unclear, patient unsure of dosage)
2. Eliquis
3. Numbing medicine (from prior provider)
4. Neck pill (from prior provider)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a veteran. Lives with female companion who assists with medication management. Uses wheelchair.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Elderly white gentleman presenting in wheelchair, no apparent distress. Cervical spine non-tender. Mildly restricted cervical extension. Symmetric right and left lateral rotation with mild lateral neck pain but no radicular pain. Spurling's maneuver benign. Bilateral biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes all 1+ and negative. Hand strength intact bilaterally with ability to squeeze examiner's fingers. Sensation symmetric in bilateral hands. Gait not assessed.

RESULTS
Cervical X-ray: Significant disc degeneration at C5-6, with lower extent at C4-5 and C3-4. Significant lower cervical facet arthropathy at C6-7 and C7-T1, though C7-T1 difficult to visualize on current films.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy, with possible contribution from peripheral neuropathy - Suspect flare of cervical radiculopathy. Will order cervical MRI to determine exact location of nerve root compression. Plan for left C7-T1 epidural injection with focused anti-inflammatory medication pending MRI results. Continue home exercise program. Continue gabapentin twice daily. Patient denies use of blood thinners. Follow up after epidural to assess symptom relief.
